bull.b: Rapid DTC growth strengthens customer relationships, brand control, and margin mix while reducing reliance on third-party retail partners. Its rising share of sales gives On a durable channel advantage that can support profitability and reinvestment as the business expands globally.

Broad-based double-digit growth alongside a 65.4% quarterly gross margin indicates that demand is scaling without sacrificing premium economics. Management’s full-year targets for low-20s constant-currency growth and at least 65% gross margin reinforce the strength of the operating model.

A growing net cash position provides substantial financial flexibility to fund stores, innovation, and international expansion without depending heavily on new borrowing. Combined with recent strong operating and free cash flow, this strengthens On’s ability to absorb volatility while pursuing growth.

bear.b: Slower wholesale growth and promotional conditions indicate that some retail partners are not selling through On products at the desired pace. Although management is protecting full-price positioning, continued channel weakness could constrain near-term revenue cadence and complicate inventory planning.

Inventory growth materially above the stated sales pace requires careful execution as wholesale sell-in is deliberately calibrated. If sell-through remains uneven, higher stock could tie up working capital or require additional promotions, potentially diluting the premium positioning that supports On’s margins.

Higher U.S. import tariffs create ongoing uncertainty for product economics and cash timing, particularly while refunds remain anticipated rather than realized. This external cost pressure could challenge margin delivery or require price and sourcing decisions that affect demand across an important market.
